title: Skill Germination: 7-day Onramp & Shadow Plan
content:
Purpose:
This is a compact, low-lift 7-day onramp and shadowing plan designed for early-stage hires (IC, junior-mid engineers, product roles) where we want to accelerate role fit signals without overwhelming managers. The goal is to produce deterministic evidence for a hire decision by day 7 and give the new hire a clear, small set of wins so they feel competent and useful.

Context and constraints (notes to self):
- Use for hires who already passed core interviews but need faster operational onboarding (trial hires, internal transfers, early grads).
- Not a replacement for full 30/60/90; a bootstrap.
- Emphasize observable work: micro-tasks, shadow calls, pair-program slots, and a short experiential assignment (<=4 hours).
- Keep cognitive load low: max 3 priorities each day.
- Track signals: technical skill, collaboration, communication, speed of learning, and reliability.

How to use this doc:
- People Ops creates onboarding packet and schedules shadow blocks.
- Hiring manager owns assignment + evidence capture.
- Buddy (peer) records 3 observations per day and shares async in the "first-week-spotlight" thread.

Day 0 (pre-arrival checklist) — completed before first day:
- Access: Slack, GitHub, JIRA, dev cluster read-only, calendar invites (meeting blocks reserved).
- Hardware: laptop imaged and tested, VPN and KMS access requested, external dev env access confirmed.
- Paperwork: payroll, NDAs, IT security checklist completed.
- Send welcome note: 1) short team intro, 2) agenda for week, 3) first micro-task link.

Day 1 — Orientation and micro-onboarding (heavy human contact, low output demand)
- Morning 30m: manager welcome, role expectations, immediate priorities (top 3).
- 60m: buddy pairing session — tour of repo, dev flow, common commands, local run. Buddy documents 5 quick tips in the new hire doc.
- Afternoon: shadow meeting(s) (product standup + 1 working sync). New hire observes, takes notes, posts 3 clarifying questions to Slack thread.
- Deliverable: complete environment sanity checklist and open the micro-task issue (ticket created for evidence).

Day 2 — Guided small task + pairing
- Morning pairing: 2-hour pair on the micro-task with buddy/peer. Manager joins the first 15 minutes to align on acceptance criteria.
- Afternoon: independent progress on task + short doc summarizing approach (1 page).
- Signal targets: writes coherent approach, asks clarifying questions, uses repo CI.
- Deliverable: PR or staged patch that builds locally and includes basic tests or smoke steps.

Day 3 — Shadow deeper, cross-discipline syncs
- Morning: shadow debugging session or incident review (30–60m).
- Midday: 30m cross-functional intro (product/designer/infra) — get context on customer-facing priorities.
- Afternoon: continue micro-task iteration and start a second tiny exploratory ticket (ownership probe).
- Deliverable: updated PR feedback addressed or short playbook note in team docs.

Day 4 — Independent ownership probe
- Independent sprint: new hire owns a ~2–4 hour ticket that requires finding context, calling one person, and shipping a small, safe change (docs, tests, config).
- Pair-check at EOD: buddy spends 30m reviewing the shipped change and documents friction.
- Manager: 15m sync to review signals against rubric.
- Deliverable: merged doc/update or small merged change.

Day 5 — Communication and delivery focus
- Customer-facing context: read 1 customer bug/feedback thread and summarize implications.
- Demo: 15-minute show-and-tell of the week’s work to manager and buddy; record quick Loom if helpful.
- Deliverable: 1 short doc (why this matters) + link to PRs.

Day 6 — Consolidate and expand
- Small stretch task: pick a related low-risk improvement (performance linter, config tweak, small infra cleanup).
- Peer feedback: collect 3 notes from cross-team peers (async).
- Manager: 20m review to align on next-30-day plan draft.
- Deliverable: ticket queued for next sprint, 30-day plan draft posted to the hire folder.

Day 7 — Decision window and acceptance flow
- Evidence review: manager + buddy + people-ops review the week’s signals using the rubric below.
- Recommendation: manager writes a short decision memo (Accept / Continue probation / Reject) with supporting evidence.
- Candidate check-in: 30m with manager to share feedback, next steps, and any remediation plan if needed.

Role-fit diagnostic checklist (daily signal categories):
- Technical craft: repo familiarity, test competence, CI usage, code hygiene.
- Problem decomposition: clarity of approach and scoped work.
- Communication: async clarity, timely responses, meeting participation.
- Collaboration: pair flow, seeking help, offering ideas.
- Reliability: on-time deliverables, follow-through on actions.
- Curiosity & learning velocity: how quickly they close knowledge gaps.

Scoring rubric (simple 0/1/2 per category each day):
0 = Not observed / negative signal
1 = Some competency, inconsistent or requires coaching
2 = Clear competency and independent contribution
- Day 7 decision guideline: total >= 10 (Accept), 7–9 (Continue probation + targeted tasks), <=6 (Reject or extend trial with specific remediation).

Interview rubric snippets to reuse for future hires (compact):
- System design micro (15m): can candidate break a feature into 3 chunks and give testable acceptance criteria? Look for explicit trade-offs and a rollout plan.
- Debugging probe (10m): give them a failing test or log excerpt; do they form a hypothesis quickly and propose an experiment?
- Communication check (5m): ask them to explain their micro-task to a PM; listen for audience adaptation.

Evidence capture templates (manager/buddy) — use plain lines in the hire folder: 
- "Day X observation: what happened, what the hire said/did, why it matters"
- "Signal score (0/1/2 per category)"
- "Blocking issues and remediation suggestions"

Acceptance flow (if Accept):
- People Ops: finalize hiring paperwork, set compensation effective date, announce to team.
- Manager: assign 30/60/90 ownership items and set first 1:1 cadence.
- Buddy: propose a 30-day learning ladder and weekly checkpoints.

If probation extended:
- Define 14-day remediation with 3 clear tasks and success metrics.
- Daily async check-ins recorded by buddy.
- People Ops schedules midpoint calibration call.

Templates and quick messages (copy/paste):
- Manager welcome DM (short): "Hi {name}, excited to have you. Today we’ll do X,Y. For week one your top priority is to get one PR merged and post a 1-paragraph summary of it. I’ll be available at 11:00 for a quick sync."
- Buddy async note: "Observed: {x}. Suggest: {y}. Blocking: {z}."

Edge cases and open questions (to address before rolling wider):
- How to adapt if hire is remote in different timezone? (Short answer: move pair blocks to overlap hours and increase async evidence).
- What if role requires domain ramp (strict regulatory knowledge)? This 7-day approach may need domain-specific prework sent pre-hire.
- Managers may need calibration on scoring; propose a 30-minute calibration workshop and 3 sample hires (shadowing exercise).

Operational housekeeping:
- People Ops to create a shared folder template: onboarding/first-week/{candidate-name}/evidence.md
- Buddy to create "first-week-spotlight" slack thread with daily posts.
- Tag all artifacts with the hire tag for future analysis.

Metrics to track (we will measure adoption):
- % hires using 7-day onramp process (target 40% of eligible hires first quarter).
- Mean time-to-first-merge for hires in program.
- Hiring decision distribution at day 7 (Accept/Probation/Reject).

Next steps (action items assigned):
- Aisha: draft the Confluence page and folder templates (target 2025-11-20).
- Diego: create the new hire ticket template in Jira (JIRA-HIRE-1427) and a webhook to create the evidence folder.
- Lina: run a 30-minute manager calibration session (invite list: hiring managers for Q4 hires).

Notes to self / freeform brainstorming:
- Could pair this with a small stipend for buddy time to encourage deeper pairing.
- Consider a lightweight 20-question competency checklist to be completed by the buddy each day (quick UI).
- If this works, expand to a 3-day quick probe for contractors and a 14-day deep probe for senior ICs.

References and links (copy these into confluence later):
- Hiring signal taxonomy (internal doc id: HS-TAX-002)
summary: One-page working plan to run a deterministic 7-day onramp for new hires with clear deliverables, a simple rubric, and a decision flow at day 7. Draft for people-ops and hiring managers to pilot in Q4 2025.
